question: What is the primary goal of problem solving in nursing practice?
explanation: Every action a midwife takes, including solving unexpected clinical problems, aims to make sure the patient gets better safely. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why do midwives in low-resource settings need strong problem-solving skills?

options.A: To avoid documenting patient care entirely
options.B: To handle unexpected equipment shortages safely
options.C: To diagnose rare diseases without laboratory tests
options.D: To replace the hospital management team

explanation: Resource limitations mean midwives must frequently adapt standard procedures while keeping care safe and effective. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h1)

question: What does critical thinking in clinical practice mainly involve?
explanation: You're doing great! Critical thinking just means looking deeper at your patient's signs and symptoms instead of just accepting things at face value. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h2)

question: A first-time pregnant mum at 36 weeks suddenly has a severe headache and blurred vision. What should your clinical reasoning make you watch out for?
explanation: Spot on! Headaches and vision changes late in pregnancy are classic warning signs of dangerous blood pressure spikes that need quick action. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the very first step in any structured problem-solving framework?
explanation: You cannot solve an issue effectively until you accurately identify and understand what is actually going wrong. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h3)

question: Why is the evaluation phase necessary after implementing a solution?

options.A: To see if the patient's condition actually improved
options.B: To increase the length of the patient folder
options.C: To punish staff who made mistakes
options.D: To prove that doctors are unnecessary

explanation: Evaluation closes the loop by checking whether your chosen action solved the original issue or if you need to try something else. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which of these helps good clinical problem-solving instead of blocking it?

options.C: Adequate rest and clear handover protocols
options.D: Fatigue from long and demanding shifts

explanation: You've got this! Proper rest and clear communication help your brain work at its best, while tiredness and bias make problem-solving harder. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why is confirmation bias dangerous when caring for patients?

options.A: Writing too many notes in the patient chart
options.B: Cleaning equipment more often than required
options.C: Asking senior doctors for help too frequently
options.D: Ignoring new signs that point to a different diagnosis

explanation: Confirmation bias is when we only see what we expect to see. It can trick us into missing important changes in our patient's condition! [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h4)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?
explanation: SBAR is a standardized communication framework used to report critical patient updates clearly and concisely to other health professionals. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h5)

question: A midwife notices a mum bleeding heavily after birth and wants to call the doctor using SBAR. What should she mention first?

options.A: Her own personal complaints about the night shift
options.B: The current situation regarding the heavy bleeding
options.C: The exact price of the prescribed medications

explanation: Brilliant! The SBAR framework always starts with the immediate 'Situation' so the doctor knows right away how urgent things are. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h5)
